intro: Word for facilities managers on Mac covers the documents that run the job: checklists, notices, reports and asset labels. You can save reusable templates, build tables and print labels without extra software. Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac, helps while you work. Hold ⌥⌘, ask where a menu is, and it circles the spot on screen.
tldr: Save a checklist or notice once with File > Save as Template, then reuse it from File > New from Template.
Print asset tags and room labels from Mailings > Labels > Options, matched to the Avery product number on the box.
Apply heading styles to long reports so the table of contents builds itself.
Lazur points, guides and drafts inside Word. It does not click buttons or edit files for you.
Keep Word updated. Microsoft's October 14, 2026 release (16.114) fixed 13 Word security issues.

blocks.text: Facilities work produces paper all day. Work orders, inspection checklists, vendor notices, room bookings and asset tags all start as a document. Word for Mac is usually already open for those jobs, so it pays to set it up properly once.
What facilities managers use Word for each week

Most facilities documents repeat. The same inspection form goes out every month. The same notice goes to tenants whenever the lift is down. Word handles repeat documents well, as long as you build the master once and copy it each time.

Word is a poor fit for live tracking. A list of open jobs, with owners and due dates, belongs in a work order system or a spreadsheet. Use Word for the documents people read, sign, print or send. Use a system of record for anything you need to filter, count or assign.
Set up Word for Mac before you build anything

Start with updates. Microsoft's release notes list Word for Mac build 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026. Between September 16 and October 27, 2026, the Word entries list quality and performance fixes only. They show no new features and no menu changes.

The last Word for Mac feature entry in those notes is dated July 15, 2025. It adds a Copilot icon in the document margin. So the menus you learn this year should stay where they are. Check the release notes when a menu looks different, since the notes list changes that affect menus.
Check these three settings before you build any templates.

items: Primary language. Changing the primary language in macOS makes Word create a new Normal template and back up the old one as a file named Normal.dotm-(number).
Template folder. Go to Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations, select User templates, then click Modify.
Default font. Pick your house font once, then build templates on top of it. The [default font guide](/how-to/change-the-default-font-in-word) covers the steps.

blocks.title: Keep a copy of your Normal template
blocks.text: Before you change the primary language, copy your current Normal template somewhere safe. Word backs it up, then creates a new one. Open a test document and check your styles before you trust the new template with a real work order.
Build templates for work orders, checklists and notices

A template holds the parts you never retype. Put the logo, the header, the table layout and the sign-off block in place. Leave blanks for the details that change each time. Then save the file as a template, not as a normal document.

Save a template on Mac with File > Save as Template. Enter a name. Choose Microsoft Word template (.dotx). Choose .dotm instead if the file has macros. Then click Save. Microsoft's steps cover Word for Microsoft 365, Word 2024 and Word 2021 for Mac.

items: Open a clean copy of the checklist or notice you use most.
Delete sample names, dates and room numbers. Keep the boxes and headings.
Go to File > Save as Template and enter a name that says what the form is for.
Choose Microsoft Word template (.dotx), or .dotm if the form has macros, then click Save.
Close the file. Never type a real job into the template itself.

blocks.text: To start a new document from the template, go to File > New from Template. Fill in the copy. Save the copy under a name with the job number. Your master stays clean for the next job.

Word saves user templates by default in ~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/User Content/Templates. To reach that folder in Finder, press ⌘⇧G and paste the path. Templates you save with File > Save as Template land in that folder.

To change where Word looks for templates, go to Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations, select User templates, and click Modify. After a move, open a new document from the template to test it. A template that opens on one Mac may not be where a colleague expects it.

To retire a template, open the Templates folder in Finder and move the file to the Trash. Do this when the form changes, and save the new version under a new name first so nobody loses the old one by accident.

blocks.text: Print asset tags and room labels with Avery templates

If you print asset tags or room labels, Word can handle the layout. You do not need a separate label app for a sheet of labels. Find the product number printed on the box, then match Word to it before you type a single label.

items: Go to Mailings > Labels > Options.
Under Label products, choose the brand, such as Avery.
Pick the Product number that matches the sheet in your hand.
If the labels are a custom size, select New Label and enter the measurements.
Choose Full page of the same label to fill a sheet, or Single label for one tag.
Click Print to send it, or New Document to check the layout first.

blocks.text: Test on plain paper first. Print one sheet on paper, hold it over a label sheet against a window, and compare the edges. A misaligned test costs one sheet of paper. A misaligned run costs a full sheet of labels, and a wrong tag on an asset is harder to fix later.

For room numbers that change, use a mail merge rather than retyping each label. The [mail merge guide](/how-to/create-a-mail-merge-in-word) walks through the data source step, which is the step to check most closely.
Format long reports so readers can find things

A long report fails when nobody can find the section they need. The fix is styles, not extra spacing. Apply Heading 1 to chapter titles and Heading 2 to sections. Word then knows the structure of the document, and the table of contents can build itself from it.

Manual bold text does not appear in a table of contents. Set the look you want in the style, not by highlighting each heading. The [heading styles guide](/how-to/apply-heading-styles-in-word) shows the steps, and the [table of contents guide](/how-to/insert-a-table-of-contents-in-word) covers the rest.

Add page numbers and a header with the report name and date. The [page numbers guide](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-word) and the [header guide](/how-to/add-a-header-in-word) cover the steps. Use a watermark, such as DRAFT, while a report is still under review. The [watermark guide](/how-to/add-a-watermark-in-word) explains how.
Tables for registers, schedules and inspection results

Asset registers, service schedules and inspection results all sit best in tables. Go to Insert > Table and choose the number of columns you need. Keep one row for each item and one column for each field, such as location, condition and next due date.

Think about a fire door check across a building. Each door gets one row. Columns record the door location, its condition and the action needed. Anyone reading the report can scan down a column and see where the trouble sits.
Set the top row to repeat on each page, so a reader on page three still knows what each column means. Keep text short inside cells. Long sentences make a table hard to scan.
Share, compare and protect what leaves your desk

Reports often go to contractors, auditors and tenants. Send a PDF when you do not want anyone to edit the content. The [save as PDF guide](/how-to/save-as-a-pdf-in-word) covers the Mac steps for Word.

Compare two versions when a contractor returns a marked-up scope. Use the [compare guide](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word) to find the right menu for your version of Word. Check the result line by line before you accept a change.

Protect any document that holds tenant details or contractor pricing. The [password guide](/how-to/password-protect-a-document-in-word) explains the steps. Store the password outside the file, in your team's password manager, not on a sticky note.
If a draft disappears, check the [recovery guide](/how-to/recover-an-unsaved-document-in-word) before you retype it. Retyping a long inspection report is slow work, so check first.
A worked example: a monthly fire door checklist
Say you inspect fire doors every month across a building. You want one form that the team fills in on a Mac, prints, signs and files. Here is the full build, from a blank page to a monthly copy.

items: Open a blank document. Type the title, the building name and the inspection month at the top.
Go to Insert > Table. Add columns for door location, door ID, condition, gap seen and action needed.
Apply Heading 1 to the title and Heading 2 to any section names, so the file has a clear structure.
Go to File > Save as Template, name it for the inspection, and save it as a .dotx file.
Each month, go to File > New from Template, fill in the table, and save the copy with the month in its name.
Export a PDF for the file, and keep the Word copy for edits.

blocks.text: The master stays the same while the details change. That is the whole point of a template. A new team member can open a copy and see exactly what to fill in, without asking which version is current.

Edge case: a contractor sends back a marked-up copy. Compare it against your master before you accept any change. Nothing should change in the form without your approval, even when the contractor means well.

blocks.title: Ask before you hunt
blocks.text: Ask Lazur where a menu is before you search for it. The circle saves time on a menu you use once in a while, such as Mailings.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Word

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud, so your hands stay on the keyboard.

Use it for three kinds of help. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Ask for a draft or an explanation, and it types or speaks the answer.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word. Lazur is a separate app, so you still make each change, which suits a document you need to control.
Dictate notes and incident reports at the cursor

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. In Word, the report or checklist fills in as you talk. Dictation suits incident notes, walkthrough findings and meeting minutes, especially when you are on site and not at a desk.

Two features cut the repeat work. Snippets hold the closing lines you use every day, such as a safety reminder or a sign-off. The personal dictionary holds asset codes, building names and vendor names that a recognizer may spell wrong. Clipboard slots keep a few blocks of text ready to paste.

blocks.title: Check codes before you send
blocks.text: Read every asset code and room number back before the document leaves your desk. Dictation is fast, but one wrong character in a fire door ID can send a contractor to the wrong door.

Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your request. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Still, keep tenant personal details out of notes you do not need.
Not sure whether dictation saves you time? The [speaking versus typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) gives you a quick comparison of your own speed.
What the numbers say about admin load

Facilities-specific data on paperwork is thin. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index found that 62% of knowledge workers struggle with too much time spent searching for information in their workday. That survey covered 31,000 full-time or self-employed workers across 31 markets. It covers office workers in general, not facilities managers.

IFMA's 2026 Facility Management Pulse reads +43 on its inaugural Workload Index. A positive reading means more professionals expect workloads to rise than fall. The report drew more than 1,400 professionals from 80 countries. IFMA's director of benchmarking put it this way: 'FM leaders face steady workload growth supported by modest budgets and constrained staffing.'

The Pulse does not report on administrative tasks or technology use. So no figure here says how many hours go to Word. What it does show is pressure on teams with limited staff. When staffing is tight, a document you build once saves more time than a faster document you rebuild each month.
Mistakes that waste time in Word

items: Editing the master template. Open a copy every time, or the next form starts with last month's details.
Using bold instead of heading styles. The table of contents then skips those headings.
Printing a full label sheet before a test print. One misaligned sheet wastes the whole sheet.
Saving a form with macros as .dotx. Choose .dotm for macros, because .dotx cannot hold them.
Changing the primary language and not checking styles afterward. Check a test document first.
Skipping updates. The October 14, 2026 release fixed 13 Word security issues.
Sending an editable Word file when a PDF was meant. Use a PDF when you do not want edits.

blocks.text: Edge cases to check before you rely on this
Lazur runs on the Mac where you hold the shortcut. Windows is planned, not available. If your team works on Windows, plan the document flow around Word files and PDFs, not around Lazur's voice help.
Microsoft's template steps cover Word for Microsoft 365, Word 2024 and Word 2021 for Mac. Microsoft's template page gives no Mac steps for Word 2019 or Word 2016, so check your version first.

Also check where a template lives before you hand it out. A template saved in one Mac's user folder does not appear on a colleague's Mac by itself. Send the file, or agree on one shared location, and test it on the other machine.
Next steps for your team

Pick the one document you retype most. Save it as a template this week, then run a test label sheet if you print tags. If you want Lazur at your side, [download Lazur](/download) for macOS. A free trial starts when you first open the app, with no credit card. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for plan details.

faq.question: Is Word for Mac free for facilities managers?
faq.answer: Word for Mac comes through Microsoft's plans, and plans can change. Current plans and prices were not verified for this page, so check Microsoft's pricing page before you buy.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Word?
faq.answer: Lazur works alongside Word. It sees your screen while you hold the shortcut, points at menus, guides you one click at a time, and types or dictates text at your cursor. It does not click for you, and it is not an add-in for Word.

faq.question: Can Lazur fill in a Word form for me?
faq.answer: Lazur can draft text and type it at the cursor, and dictation can fill in what you say. Lazur does not edit files or operate Word for you, so you still enter each field and save the file.

faq.question: Does Lazur store the documents I work on?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did on your Mac.

faq.question: Which Word versions do the template and label steps cover?
faq.answer: Microsoft's template steps cover Word for Microsoft 365, Word 2024 and Word 2021 for Mac. Its Avery label steps cover the same three versions. Microsoft's template page gives no Mac steps for Word 2019 or Word 2016.

faq.question: Why update Word if the release notes show no new features?
faq.answer: The October 14, 2026 release (16.114) lists 13 Word security fixes. Security fixes matter for files that hold tenant details or contractor pricing. Install the update when Microsoft ships it, then restart Word.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac, and it runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: What is the difference between .dotx and .dotm?
faq.answer: Both are Word template formats. Use .dotx for a plain template. Use .dotm when the template has macros, because .dotx cannot hold them.
